title: PrimeVul paired functions: a vulnerable function and its patch
decision: whether a C/C++ function contains a security vulnerability (asked for the vulnerable and for the patched version of the same function)

source.name: PrimeVul: Vulnerability Detection with Code Language Models: How Far Are We? (ICSE 2025, arXiv:2403.18624)
files: primevul_test_paired.jsonl (README link "Original Release": Google Drive folder 19iLaNDS0z99N8kB_jBRTmDLehwZBolMY, file 1rNDKb65Yn1rCBURzHeBcH4jVVdQ1oD4r, sha256 54a16a5ab663d11d1ffa5f48a98b0f996e82ee85f48a2b999334f6c1a7d96e41)
source.split: paired test, original release (564 pairs = 1,128 functions)

notes: 564 pairs in the file (the paired test set of the paper); 54 pairs with a function longer than 12,000 characters dropped, 510 left, 500 sampled (seed 20261007). Two rows per pair with a shared group: the function before the security fix (gold yes) and the same function after it (gold no); a group counts only if both rows are right, so one answer for every row scores 0 and independent guessing scores 0.25. Labels are automatic (functions changed by vulnerability-fixing commits): no means that the known flaw was fixed, not that the function was audited. 2 patched functions (source idx 349259, 439495) are listed by the source in two pairs each and both pairs were sampled: these rows occur twice, under separate ids and groups. The repository also offers a re-release v0.1 with CVE metadata whose paired test set has 435 pairs (870 rows, the size listed in datasets_verified.md from a third-party copy); it is not used here. The functions are C/C++ code from open-source projects (Linux, TensorFlow, vim, ...), which keep their own licences; the data set itself is released under the MIT License. Decontamination against the training data of the final StartLux-Decision-27B (scan of 10 October 2026, 3,252,020 training records of Stage 1, Stage 2, Stage 3 and the RL pool): 4 of 1000 items removed because a text field of the item occurs in it; 996 items remain.
